source.snippet: I have a Salesforce → Google Calendar integration built on a 2nd-gen External Credential / Named Credential, and the stored OAuth token silently stops refreshing anywhere from ~1.5 hours to ~2 days after a successful authentication, even though everything appears correctly configured and Google's own audit log shows no revocation event. Setup Auth Provider: Provider Type = Google, PKCE enabled, Default Scopes = openid profile email https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar...

problem_statement: Salesforce integrations using 2nd-gen External Credentials with Google OAuth silently lose their refresh tokens after hours to days, breaking calendar and other Google Workspace integrations with no clear error or audit trail.
target_segment: Salesforce admins and developers at companies integrating Salesforce with Google Workspace (Calendar, Drive, etc.)
notes: Professional business context: developer/admin at a company maintaining a live Salesforce-Google Calendar integration. The silent failure mode (no error, no audit event) makes debugging extremely time-consuming — a monitoring or auto-remediation tool for Salesforce OAuth credential health could have recurring B2B value. Single signal; score capped at 2 pending corroboration.
